topics.title: Nor'easter floods Northeast coast
topics.summary: A slow-moving nor'easter brought coastal flooding, strong winds, power outages, travel delays, and event disruptions across parts of the U.S. Northeast, with forecasters warning rough conditions could continue Sunday.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the weather ruins everybody's plans, who becomes the emergency planner and who insists the show can still go on?

topics.title: U.S. and China add AI safety channel
topics.summary: China and the United States agreed to create a channel for AI-related incidents, continue military crisis communication work, extend a trade truce, and meet again at upcoming international summits.
topics.discussionPrompt: If two rivals open an AI hotline, who trusts the paperwork and who wants to know what counts as an AI emergency?

topics.title: Iran pushes diplomacy after rejected plan
topics.summary: Iran said diplomacy remains the path forward after President Trump rejected its proposal tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, sanctions relief, oil sales, and a wider ceasefire.
topics.discussionPrompt: When one side says diplomacy is still possible after a hard no, who sees an opening and who hears a door slam?

topics.title: Hawaii watches Hurricane Nolo
topics.summary: Hurricane Nolo passed south of Hawaii's Big Island, but officials warned it could still bring flash flooding, dangerous surf, and strong winds to areas recovering from earlier storms.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a storm misses the island but still causes trouble, who relaxes too early and who keeps checking every forecast map?

topics.title: Swiss voters keep flexible neutrality
topics.summary: Swiss voters rejected a proposal for stricter neutrality rules that would have limited cooperation with NATO and narrowed Switzerland's ability to join sanctions or partnerships.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a country votes on what neutrality should mean, who wants a strict rulebook and who prefers room to maneuver?

topics.title: Pope Leo draws huge Paris crowd
topics.summary: Pope Leo XIV drew a Vatican-estimated 800,000 people to an outdoor Mass on Paris' Champs-Elysees before continuing his visit with a trip to Lourdes.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a public event pulls a crowd bigger than expected, who studies the logistics and who just wants to know where everyone parked?

topics.title: Bangkok recovers from floodwaters
topics.summary: Floodwaters receded in many parts of Bangkok after torrential rain, while residents assessed losses and Thai officials approved special civil-service holidays for Bangkok and nearby provinces.
topics.discussionPrompt: After city flooding, who starts cleaning immediately and who begins a full investigation into the drainage system?

topics.title: Kennedy Center repairs questioned
topics.summary: Former Kennedy Center employees alleged officials delayed planned repair work despite known structural issues, while the venue says newer investigations found safety risks behind its temporary closure.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a famous venue closes over safety concerns, who asks about the engineering and who asks what happens to all the performances?

topics.title: Ukraine mobile provider hit
topics.summary: Kyivstar, Ukraine's largest mobile service provider, said its headquarters was hit as Russia continued strikes on logistics, port, transport, and data infrastructure.
topics.discussionPrompt: When communications infrastructure becomes part of a conflict, who worries about daily life first and who focuses on backup plans?

topics.title: International NFL schedule expands
topics.summary: The NFL's international schedule includes a record nine regular-season games across seven countries and four continents, with Baltimore and Dallas set for Rio de Janeiro on Sept. 27.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your team plays halfway around the world, who calls it exciting growth and who worries about jet lag ruining everything?
